title: Jump Game II
statement: nums[i] is the maximum jump length from index i. Starting at index 0, return the minimum number of jumps needed to reach the last index. The last index is always reachable.

hints.1_question: Think in 'waves': from the current wave of positions, how far could one more jump take you?
hints.2_nudge: Track the farthest index reachable so far and the end of the current jump's range. When you reach that end, you must jump again.
hints.3_big_hint: for i in range(n-1): far = max(far, i + nums[i]); if i == cur_end: jumps += 1; cur_end = far.

known_bugs.name: always takes the full jump of the current cell
known_bugs.followup: Is jumping as far as possible from where you stand always best, or should you consider where each landing spot can take you next?

known_bugs.name: loop includes the last index (counts an extra jump)
known_bugs.followup: Do you need another jump once you are already standing on the last index?

known_bugs.name: dynamic programming over every pair (O(n^2))
known_bugs.followup: How many (i, j) updates happen when every cell can jump far? Is there a way to keep only the farthest reach?

followups: Why is this greedy equivalent to a BFS over levels?
What if some jumps could go backwards?
